findings.problem: The Venice printing reads 'Quae est ista vestis? Christus.', printed with long s and the st ligature as 'Quæ eſt iſta veſtis? Chriſtus.' It stands at printed p. 282, left column, line 11, which is page 5 of the retained facsimile matthew-22-facsimile-d80cea1b (SHA-256 d80cea1b..., verified). Operator intervention 0001 asked for this reading to be settled. I settled it from the page's native 1807x2500 one-bit text layer and from a 1200-dpi render, by comparing column-top profiles. The questioned letters match the st ligature of 'est' and 'vestis' on the same line: a curved long-s shoulder well below the ascender line, rising to a peak that arches right into a t whose crossbar sits at x-height. They do not match the genuine 'll' of 'illum' lower in the same column, whose two separate stems both rise flat-topped to full ascender height with no crossbar. At reduced scale the ligature imitates 'll': 'Christum induistis' five lines below looks like 'Chrillum'. The registered OCR reads this very line 'Quae ell ilia veftis? Chrillus', turning every st ligature in it into 'll'. The accepted expansive study prints 'ista' correctly ('what is this garment?'), and study-review's accepted STU-017 already records that the page reads 'ista'. Synthesis-review iteration 0 misread the page, its SYN-002 instruction to quote 'illa' was wrong, and the repair followed it. The concise study now misquotes Aquinas's Latin at the exact locus it cites. That quotation is a new, false source-dependent claim which departs from the accepted study's checked quotation, and the production audit records a facsimile check that reached the wrong reading. The rest of the SYN-002 repair is correct against the page and should stand.
findings.required_result: Print the question as \latin{Quae est ista vestis? Christus}, glossed as the expansive study glosses it ('what is this garment? Christ'). Leave the rest of the repaired sentence and the later comparison as they are. Make research/production-review.md state that the Venice page reads 'ista', and withdraw the iteration-1 statements that it reads 'illa', including the 'For the cold reviewer' note that reports the expansive study's 'ista' as a discrepancy. Describe the derive-synthesis contributions accurately in generation-metadata.tex. Do not edit the expansive study, whose reading is correct.

summary: Cold review, iteration 1, of the concise study (synthesis.tex; 12 physical pages). All 15 sealed input hashes match. I rebuilt it independently from those sources: it settles in two passes, its aux is byte-identical to the author's proof (9fa9be30...), the extracted text is identical, the log has no box or LaTeX warning, all 16 fonts are embedded, and the zref markers fall on p. 1 (inventory and four sense rows), p. 2 (chronology), pp. 3-4 (themes) and p. 5 (commentary). I read everything that moved: themes, commentary, apparatus, the generation record and the production audit. SYN-001 is repaired: no other Mass of Schuster's is named. SYN-002's substantive repair is correct against Venice p. 282: the four ways are given distributively, and 'et si unum deficiat, malum' governs only the closing triad, which is quoted exactly. Advisories SYN-003 to SYN-006 are cleared, and Chrysostom's new quotations match NPNF 1/10 Homily 69 verbatim. On operator intervention 0001, I settled the reading from the native 1807x2500 text layer of facsimile page 5 and a 1200-dpi render, comparing stem profiles with 'est' and 'vestis' on the same line and with the genuine 'll' of 'illum' on the page. The page reads 'Quae est ista vestis?'. Synthesis-review 0 misread it, and the concise study now prints 'illa', so one finding blocks: SYN-009, owner synthesis. SYN-007 still stands with the research owner. SYN-008's premise is false; it is recorded as an observation for a person to retire. Limits: no other edition of Super Matthaeum was consulted for the demonstrative, and unchanged pages were read in the rebuilt text and contact sheet without re-verifying their sources. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED.
